hints.content:
The graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ can be transformed
to get the graph of $y=2\sqrt{x+2}$. 
[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Suppose $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=2\sqrt{x+2}$.  

>$\begin{align}f(x)&=\sqrt{x}\\\\
f(x+2)&=\sqrt{x+2}\\\\
2f(x+2)&=2\sqrt{x+2}\\\\
\end{align}$

Notice that what is on the right-hand side of the equal sign is $g(x)$.  Therefore, $g(x)=2f(x+2)$.  

Since function $g$ can be built from function $f$, the graph of function $g$ is a transformation of the graph of function $f$.

hints.content:
Replacing $x$ with $x+2$ shifts the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ left $2$ units.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A square root function graph and a shifted graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint at (zero, zero) and passes through (four, two). The shifted graph has an endpoint at (negative two, zero) and passes through (two, two).

hints.content:
Multiplying $\sqrt{x+2}$ by $2$ stretches the graph of $y=\sqrt{x+2} $ vertically by a factor of $2$.  

[[☃ image 1]]

Note that the graph of the function passes through $(2,2)$ *before* the stretch, and $(2, 4 )$ *after* the stretch.  This is because each $y$-coordinate is multiplied by $2$.  

Additionally it is important to follow order of operations when building the function, as function transformations are not always commutative.  [[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Consider the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$.

If we shift the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ down $2$ units, and then reflect this across the $x$-axis, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, two) and passes through (ten, negative one).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/838d19b306cd3a25ac6c67be671bb6a26eaf0e71)

However, if we first reflect the graph of $y=\sqrt{x}$ across the $x$-axis and then shift this graph down $2$ units, we get the following graph.

![A square root function graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint (zero, negative two) and passes through (ten, negative five).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/76bbee52d28bfb5f5bcd72a6831a797eaab9824d)

These graphs are not the same, indicating that the order in which you perform the transformations is important!

options.alt: A square root function graph and its vertically stretched graph on an x y coordinate plane. It has an endpoint at (negative two, zero) and passes through (two, two). The vertically stretched graph has an endpoint at (negative two, zero) and passes through (two, four).
